provision: Establishes GHG reduction targets for each MPO, but targets are non-binding and vary by region
california_gap: Targets lack enforceability; MPOs face no penalty for missing targets
recommended_language: Amend to require CARB to impose enforceable backstop measures when MPO Sustainable Communities Strategies fail to achieve adopted targets.

provision: CARB certifies Sustainable Communities Strategies but has limited enforcement tools
california_gap: No financial or regulatory consequence for non-compliance
recommended_language: Add a performance-based funding linkage: MPOs that fail to meet interim VMT benchmarks lose eligibility for discretionary state transportation funds.

provision: SCS must consider GHG impacts but equity analysis is discretionary
california_gap: No mandatory anti-displacement or environmental justice screen in SCS
recommended_language: Require each SCS to include a Displacement Risk Analysis and demonstrate net benefit to disadvantaged communities, consistent with AB 1550.

provision: CARB monitors aggregate statewide VMT but link-level or CBG-level reporting is not required
california_gap: Limited granularity hinders identifying lagging regions
recommended_language: Mandate annual VMT monitoring at the Census Block Group level using the Caltrans VMTIndex methodology, with public dashboard reporting.

provision: RHNA cycle aligned with SCS cycle, but zoning override authority is weak
california_gap: Local zoning can frustrate SCS land-use projections
recommended_language: Grant limited zoning pre-emption authority to MPOs for transit-rich housing opportunity areas identified in the adopted SCS.

provision: No dedicated transportation demand management (TDM) fund tied to SB 375 outcomes
california_gap: Lack of stable TDM funding undermines VMT reduction programs
recommended_language: Establish a VMT Reduction Trust Fund seeded by a portion of Cap-and-Trade transportation revenues, distributed based on verified per-capita VMT reductions.

provision: SB 21-260 sets statewide GHG reduction targets (26% below 2005 by 2025; 50% by 2030) with legal backstop
california_gap: Colorado's targets are codified in statute with CDOT accountable
recommended_language: Adopt Colorado-style enforceable statewide VMT/GHG targets for the transportation sector with CARB backstop authority.

provision: CDOT must submit annual GHG reduction plans; failure triggers automatic rulemaking
california_gap: Automatic regulatory trigger removes political discretion
recommended_language: Model an automatic rulemaking trigger in CARB if transportation GHG exceeds the annual target trajectory by more than 3%.

provision: CDOT GHG Program uses link-level traffic data with annual public reporting
california_gap: Granular public reporting enables accountability
recommended_language: Require Caltrans to publish an annual Transportation GHG Dashboard at the route / segment level using CT-EMFAC and PeMS data.

provision: GWSA requires statewide GHG reductions of 50% by 2030 and net zero by 2050; transportation sector has sub-targets
california_gap: Sub-sector targets prevent over-reliance on non-transport reductions
recommended_language: Disaggregate California's 2045 carbon neutrality goal into sector-level sub-targets, with transportation holding at least a 45% share.

provision: MassDEP issues binding regulations (310 CMR 60.05) with civil penalty authority
california_gap: Regulatory authority backed by civil penalties
recommended_language: Authorize CARB civil penalties against MPOs that miss consecutive SCS interim milestones.

provision: Environmental justice communities receive enhanced monitoring and first-priority mitigation measures
california_gap: Explicit EJ community protections are mandated by regulation
recommended_language: Require California MPOs to allocate ≥25% of VMT-reduction funding to SB 535 Disadvantaged Community projects.

provision: Annual Transportation Sector GHG Report published by MassDEP using observed traffic data
california_gap: Observed (not modeled) data used for compliance verification
recommended_language: Transition California's SB 375 performance tracking from modeled SCS projections to observed VMT data (PeMS + StreetLight).

provision: MnDOT GHG Assessment identifies a 75% GHG reduction target for transportation by 2050
california_gap: Long-term statutory transportation target provides investment certainty
recommended_language: Add a 2050 net-zero VMT-intensity target for California's transportation sector to complement 2035 SCS targets.

provision: MnDOT publishes annual GHG assessment using MOVES model, with scenario modeling
california_gap: Scenario modeling helps evaluate policy options before adoption
recommended_language: Require CARB to publish annual scenario analyses showing projected VMT and GHG outcomes under different land-use and pricing policy alternatives.

provision: Tribal and rural communities included in GHG planning process with dedicated outreach
california_gap: Explicit rural / tribal inclusion fills a gap in urban-centric SB 375
recommended_language: Expand SB 375 applicability to non-MPO regions with a rural VMT-reduction framework administered by Caltrans.

provision: SMART Scale uses a data-driven, transparent scoring algorithm for project prioritization, weighting GHG/VMT outcomes
california_gap: Transparent scoring algorithm reduces political influence on project selection
recommended_language: Adopt a SMART Scale–style VMT-weighted scoring system for Caltrans and MPO project programming in the State Transportation Improvement Program (STIP).

provision: Projects that do not score above a minimum SMART Scale threshold are ineligible for STIP inclusion
california_gap: Hard threshold creates real consequence for high-VMT projects
recommended_language: Establish a VMT-per-dollar threshold in the STIP: projects that increase net VMT per capita are ineligible unless offset by a TDM component.

provision: Smart Scale scoring directly links transportation investment to performance outcomes including GHG
california_gap: Performance-based funding allocation reduces pork-barrel spending
recommended_language: Integrate a VMT impact score into California's Interregional Transportation Improvement Program (ITIP) project scoring.

provision: SMART Scale project performance is publicly tracked post-construction
california_gap: Post-construction outcome monitoring is rare in California
recommended_language: Require post-construction VMT monitoring for all federally funded California transportation projects >$10M, published on a state dashboard.
